m.history.EVENTS.1: .NET Framework 1.0, C# 1.0 and Visual Studio .NET are released. Windows only.
m.history.EVENTS.3: Mono 1.0: an open-source .NET implementation for Linux from Ximian (Miguel de Icaza).
m.history.EVENTS.5: Unity 1.0: a game engine with scripting on Mono.
m.history.EVENTS.6: .NET Framework 3.0: WPF, WCF and Workflow Foundation.
m.history.EVENTS.7: .NET Framework 3.5 and C# 3.0: LINQ and lambdas.
m.history.EVENTS.9: .NET Framework 4.0: the Task Parallel Library (TPL) and dynamic.
m.history.EVENTS.10: Xamarin is founded: C# for iOS and Android, built on Mono.
m.history.EVENTS.11: .NET Framework 4.5 and C# 5.0: async and await.
m.history.EVENTS.12: Microsoft goes open source: the Roslyn compiler, the .NET Foundation, and .NET Core announced under the MIT license.
m.history.EVENTS.13: C# 6.0 and the Roslyn compiler in Visual Studio 2015.
m.history.EVENTS.14: Unity ships IL2CPP: C# code is turned into C++.
m.history.EVENTS.15: Microsoft buys Xamarin and makes it free.
m.history.EVENTS.16: .NET Core 1.0: officially on Windows, Linux and macOS.
m.history.EVENTS.18: .NET Core 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.0: a huge shared set of APIs.
m.history.EVENTS.19: Unity moves to a new Mono with the .NET 4.x API and supports .NET Standard 2.0.
m.history.EVENTS.20: .NET Framework 4.8: the last major version of Framework.
m.history.EVENTS.21: .NET Core 3.0: WPF and WinForms (Windows only). C# 8: nullable reference types.
m.history.EVENTS.22: .NET Standard 2.1, the last version of the standard. Framework does not support it.
m.history.EVENTS.23: .NET 5: "Core" is dropped from the name and version 4 is skipped. C# 9: records.
m.history.EVENTS.28: Unity announces its move to CoreCLR.
m.history.EVENTS.32: Revit 2025 and AutoCAD 2025 move from Framework 4.8 to .NET 8.
m.history.EVENTS.33: Microsoft hands the Mono project over to the WineHQ community.
m.history.EVENTS.35: Support for STS releases is extended from 18 months to two years.
m.history.EVENTS.36: Support for .NET 8 and .NET 9 ends on November 10.
m.history.EVENTS.37: .NET 11 is in preview, with release expected in November.
